articles.title: Oregon's 35,132-acre Ochoco Ranch asked $65 million in 2022; four years later, the price has dropped to $54 million; the property has a 10,287-sq-ft self-sustaining lodge, three residences and 19 miles of spring-fed creeks
articles.summary: A sprawling Oregon ranch with a mountain-top lodge and more than 35,000 acres of timberland, complete with its own streams, is on the market for $54
articles.body: A sprawling Oregon ranch with a mountain-top lodge and more than 35,000 acres of timberland, complete with its own streams, is on the market for $54 million, Mansion Global reported. Ochoco Ranch first went on the market in 2022, asking $65 million, making it the most expensive property listing in the state. Earlier this year, the property returned to the market after an $11 million price cut.Oregon's most expensive propertyA recreational paradise, Ochoco Ranch spans more than 35,000 acres of timberland in Prineville, in Central Oregon. It borders the Ochoco National Forest, and Redmond Airport is about 20 miles away. Most of the trees here are ponderosa pine, white fir and Douglas fir. For decades, the land has been managed as working timberland, and it has never been a quiet weekend retreat with just a few trails.“The large deeded acreage of timbered high country comprising the Ochoco Ranch makes this an exceptional resource. This resource, combined with its excellent location near a rapidly growing area, along with the multitude of recreational possibilities, allows the Ochoco Ranch to be well positioned for future value enhancement. The property is a blank canvas, available in its raw natural form, allowing it to be taken in a variety of directions by the new owner,” Mason & Morse Ranch Co, the company that listed the ranch, said.There is a three-storey lodge at its centre. Built in 2015, the lodge sits on top of a butte, offering views across the snowy Cascade Mountains, with forest in the foreground. The lodge has nine bedrooms, eight fireplaces, exposed-beam ceilings, a library, a wine cellar and an armory vault. The house is designed to run on renewable energy and water sourced from the property itself. That is, obviously, a big part of the pitch.The property also has more homes than most buyers would expect. Two more wood-frame lodges sit on the ranch. One is off-grid, while the other is connected to the electricity grid. A three-bedroom foreman's home covers 3,000 square feet. A smaller, 2,800-square-foot house sits near a natural warm spring and has a wraparound porch and a rock fireplace.There are also workshops, equipment sheds, a woodworking shed, a six-stall horse barn, two cabins and a tower for watching for fires.A working ranch on the sideOchoco is not just a place to relax. It also operates as a timber ranch, generating income from timber sales and carbon offsets through sustainable logging practices.“It's a great legacy property for someone who wants a recreational property but also wants to generate some income,” listing agent Jake Polvi of Polvi Real Estate, who co-listed the property with John Stratman, Rue Balcomb and Robb Van Pelt of Mason & Morse, told the outlet.Also, don't mind the visitors. The ranch is home to elk, mule deer, antelope, grouse, quail and turkey. Miles of spring-fed creeks are filled with rainbow and brook trout, making the property ideal for hunting and fishing.Accessibility is another perk. “The ranch is accessed by three private easements on the primary roads. These primary roads are raised, bladed gravel roads adjoining the highway and cut through the ranch north/south and east/west. Secondary and limited-use roads cut through the property in various directions and are accessed from the primary roads. This road system makes the property readily accessible and provides a major value enhancement. A well-developed road system such as this cannot be found on comparable properties,” the listing says.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Gas stations may be hiding some of America's most overlooked affordable fast-food options
articles.summary: From Wawa's hoagies to Buc-ee's chopped brisket, these convenience store and gas station meals can be surprisingly delicious budget-friendly meals. Check out this list.
articles.body: Some people may shy away from the idea of getting a meal at a gas station or convenience store — but doing so could be an easy, and surprisingly delicious, way to save money while on a road trip or during a daily commute. Restaurant menu prices rose 0.3% in both July and August this year, and menu prices were 3.4% higher this August than in August 2025, the National Restaurant Association reported in September. "Gas stations with quick service attached to them like 7Eleven, am/pm, etc. are the real value now," a Reddit user said in a recent thread. FAST-FOOD DRIVE-THRUS TOOK OVER AMERICAN MORNINGS FOR THESE KEY REASONS "Everything has shifted upwards. Fast food is now fast casual pricing. Fast casual is now sit down restaurant pricing." Amid these increases, finding inexpensive and convenient dining options might be challenging, but it’s not impossible. Here are a few convenience store and gas station chains offering tasty, budget-friendly meals and snacks — ranging from a $5 half-foot-long sub sandwich to a $9.99 box filled to the brim with Southern comfort food. QuickChek New Jersey-based gas station and convenience chain QuickChek has more than 160 locations across New Jersey and parts of New York. Six-inch subs and sandwiches cost $5 a piece, while a $4 breakfast combo includes an English muffin or croissant breakfast sandwich and a 20-ounce hot coffee or energy drink, according to the website. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER The chain also offers a small, medium or large iced coffee for $1.99, which includes any customizations. Wawa Headquartered in Pennsylvania, Wawa serves coffee, a variety of breakfast items, snacks and freshly made sandwiches. The chain earned the top spot in the American Customer Satisfaction Index’s 2024 convenience store ranking primarily due to the chain’s food offerings, especially its hoagies. A classic Italian hoagie on a six-inch roll costs $6.29, while a breakfast meal including a breakfast sandwich, a hash brown and a coffee or fountain drink costs $5, according to the Wawa website. Buc-ee’s Since its founding in 1982, Beaver-themed gas station chain Buc-ee’s has developed a reputation for affordable gas prices, logo-adorned merchandise, and its extensive food offerings. The lower gas prices are mainly due to the fact that customers are expected to spend more money inside the store, Yahoo Finance reported in June. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS The chopped brisket sandwich is a popular grab-and-go meal option, with the standard 8-ounce size selling for less than $10 at most locations, according to a website sharing Buc-ee’s menu items and pricing information. Some Redditors say that a trip to Buc-ee’s is not complete without Beaver nuggets, a sweet, crunchy puffed corn snack. A large bag of Beaver nuggets sells for about five dollars, and the homemade fudge costs about four dollars per square, according to Southern Living. All Buc-ee’s locations are open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, according to the website, and as an added bonus, the restrooms are known for being extremely sanitary. In a Buc-ee’s thread on Reddit, a commenter said, "Be sure to check out the clean bathrooms!" Parker’s Kitchen Founded in Georgia in 1976, Parker’s Kitchen operates 110 locations across Georgia and South Carolina. Known for Southern-inspired food like fried chicken and biscuits, the gas station and convenience chain offers meal options with prices that rival those at fast-food restaurants. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ A $9.99 Fill Up Box from Parker’s Kitchen includes a small side, a drink, and the choice of three chicken tenders, a chicken sandwich, two pork chops, two pieces of fried catfish, or livers and gizzards. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The lunch menu features a $4.99 pulled pork sandwich and a $3.99 barbecue chicken sandwich, as well as a $3.99 cheeseburger, according to the website.

articles.title: A Texas family spent nearly eight years fighting over the 65,000-acre Brite Ranch, worth at least $60 million; days before trial, the heirs agreed to divide the historic property into four pieces
articles.summary: A bitter family dispute over one of West Texas’s most historic ranches has taken an unexpected turn, with the heirs agreeing to divide the sprawling
articles.body: A bitter family dispute over one of West Texas’s most historic ranches has taken an unexpected turn, with the heirs agreeing to divide the sprawling property rather than force a sale of the entire estate. The agreement involving the 65,000-acre Brite Ranch was reported by The Big Bend Sentinel on October 8, 2026, shortly before a jury trial was scheduled to begin. Court records from the Texas Court of Appeals and historical accounts published by the Texas State Historical Association provide further context on the dispute and the ranch’s legacy. The settlement brings the family closer to resolving a legal battle that began in 2018, when disagreements over trust management and the distribution of ranch income escalated into years of litigation. Valued at an estimated $60 million or more, the property has long been both a family asset and a significant part of Presidio County’s history.Four heirs, four portions of the ranchUnder the proposed settlement, the ranch would be divided into four portions for Jim White, his brother Mac White, their sister Hester Ann White and Geoffrey Connor, the adopted son of Mac and the late Beau White. The agreement marks a major shift in the dispute. Hester Ann had opposed dividing the property and sought a court-ordered sale of the ranch as a single estate. However, a filing dated October 1 requested cancellation of the jury trial scheduled for October 21 and acknowledged her agreement to the division, according to The Big Bend Sentinel.The settlement does not necessarily mean every issue has been resolved. The newspaper reported that Jim, Cuatro White, Mac and Connor had also asked the district judge to retain the proceeding as a bench trial, potentially allowing the court to consider whether the allocation of land should be adjusted. They argued that Hester Ann had not contributed to certain ranch expenses and court-related costs. At the time of the newspaper’s report, the judge had not ruled on the request.How the family dispute beganThe conflict dates to a lawsuit filed in 2018 by Mac and Beau against their brother Jim, who managed the ranch and served as trustee of the family trust that held its principal assets. The brothers alleged that Jim had breached his fiduciary duties, including by failing to distribute income fairly and by making decisions involving compensation for himself and family members working on the property. A jury trial in 2023 resulted in a judgment that removed Jim as trustee, awarded damages and divided the family trust into separate trusts. Former Texas Comptroller Susan Combs was appointed interim trustee to oversee financial administration.Jim and his supporters challenged the decision. In December 2024, the Eighth Court of Appeals in El Paso reversed the judgment and ordered a new trial, finding a fundamental error in the jury instructions. The ruling revived Jim’s position in the wider dispute and prolonged uncertainty over the ranch’s future.The litigation also became entangled in a dispute over Connor’s adoption by Mac and Beau in 2022. Some relatives challenged the adoption, alleging it was intended to affect inheritance interests. The allegations were contested, and the question of whether the adoption was improper was not resolved in the proceedings described by The Big Bend Sentinel. Years of court proceedings, disagreements over control of the land and the costs of litigation have now given way to an agreement that could finally establish separate ownership for the heirs.A ranch with more than a century of historyThe Brite Ranch was established by Lucas Charles Brite, who began accumulating land in the region in the late 19th century. The operation became known for its Hereford cattle and grew into a major ranching enterprise in the Big Bend region of Texas. At its height, the original holdings extended across substantially more land than the current 65,000-acre property.Its history also includes a violent episode that became part of the region’s broader borderlands story. On Christmas Day in 1917, armed raiders attacked the ranch, looted its store and killed civilians. The raid was followed weeks later by the Porvenir Massacre, in which Texas Rangers and other armed men killed 15 Mexican and Mexican American men and boys. Historical accounts identify the killings as retaliation linked to suspicions surrounding the earlier raid, although the victims were not established to have participated in it.For generations, the Brite family remained prominent in the civic and political life of Presidio County. The ranch consequently represents more than a valuable stretch of land: it is tied to the region’s cattle industry, local government and difficult border history. The proposed division would give the heirs separate portions of an estate that has remained at the centre of their family for decades. Whether the settlement ends the litigation will depend on the court’s handling of the outstanding issues, but the agreement signals a move away from the prospect of selling the historic ranch as a single property.You use AI every day. articles.title: Mexican president urges residents to shelter as Hurricane Simon approaches
articles.summary: The Mexican community of Cabo Corrientes faces the risk of a direct hit as the Category 4 storm churns off Jalisco.
articles.body:
Mexican President ‌‌Claudia Sheinbaum has urged residents along the Pacific Ocean to stay indoors as Hurricane Simon’s powerful winds and heavy rains pound coastal communities.

As of Sunday, the hurricane’s eye was moving offshore of Mexico’s Jalisco state, with winds of at least 240km/h (150mph).

Torrential rain has already battered residents living between the Sierra Madre mountain range and the ocean. Communities in hilly and mountainous areas have been warned to brace for mudslides.

Simon reached Category 4 strength, on a scale of five, on Saturday, as part of an unusually active Pacific hurricane season.

“With the approaching impact of Category 4 Hurricane Simon, we urge residents of coastal municipalities ‌‌in Jalisco, Colima, Nayarit and Michoacan to remain sheltered until authorities officially declare that the danger has passed,” Sheinbaum wrote in a post on the social media platform X on Sunday.

In a midday advisory , the United States’ National Hurricane Center (NHC) warned that Simon could produce “additional rainfall totals of 8 to 16 inches (20 to 41 cm) over portions of southwestern Mexico”.

Precipitation totals as high as 76 cm (30 inches) were possible in areas of Michoacan, Colima, and Jalisco until Monday.

It’s not clear whether the storm will make landfall. But the greatest risk of a direct hit lies at the moment with Cabo Corrientes, a town that sits on a cape in Jalisco, jutting into the Pacific Ocean.

Mexico’s National Civil Protection ⁠⁠Coordination (CNPC) placed 28 municipalities in Jalisco and Colima under its highest cyclone alert level, while another 93 municipalities were under a ⁠⁠high alert level, according to civil protection bulletins.

Classes were suspended in the affected areas, and efforts to evacuate residents were under way.

Businesses in popular tourist destinations like Puerto Vallarta boarded up windows and placed sandbags at entrances as the storm approached.

Jalisco’s Governor Pablo Navarro warned that the high-powered hurricane was creating “high-risk marine conditions” along the coast of his state, with waves reaching as high as eight metres (26 feet).

On Sunday, he also shared video on social media of the storm surge crashing onto sidewalks and flooding waterways.

“Here is the current state of Jalisco’s beaches this morning — from Barra de Navidad to Puerto Vallarta — as Hurricane Simon passes through,” he wrote in the video’s caption.

“I ask everyone to heed official instructions, take precautions and avoid putting themselves at risk. The safety of Jalisco’s families is the top priority.”

articles.title: In 1941, a Beverly Hills home was built for Boris Karloff; after later belonging to Gregory Peck, writers who bought it for about $2.8 million in 2003 returned the preserved estate to market for $6.5 million in 2026
articles.summary: A Beverly Hills estate with ties to two Hollywood legends has returned to the luxury property market, offering a rare glimpse into the residential history
articles.body: A Beverly Hills estate with ties to two Hollywood legends has returned to the luxury property market, offering a rare glimpse into the residential history of Old Hollywood. Built for horror-film icon Boris Karloff in 1941 and later owned by Academy Award-winning actor Gregory Peck, the property is now listed for $6.5 million by Robert Guza Jr., the former head writer of General Hospital. The listing was reported by Mansion Global in a July 2026 article by Casey Farmer, with property details attributed to listing agents Holly Hatch and Chris Johnson of Coldwell Banker Realty. Set along Mulholland Drive, the house stands apart from the contemporary mansions that have increasingly reshaped Beverly Hills. Its appeal lies not only in its celebrity connections but also in the preservation of a period home that has retained much of its original character.A home shaped by Hollywood historyThe property was originally constructed for Karloff, the British actor whose portrayal of Frankenstein’s monster in the 1931 film Frankenstein helped establish him as one of cinema’s most recognisable horror stars. He also became familiar to television audiences as the narrator and voice of the Grinch in the 1966 animated special How the Grinch Stole Christmas.Karloff subsequently sold the Cape Cod-style residence to Peck, another major figure in American cinema. Peck won the Academy Award for best actor for his portrayal of Atticus Finch in To Kill a Mockingbird and appeared in films including Roman Holiday, Spellbound and The Yearling.The house later passed to Guza and his late wife, Meg Bennett, an actress and television writer. Property records cited by Mansion Global indicate that the couple acquired it in 2003. The publication reported the current asking price at $6.5 million, although it could not independently establish the couple’s original purchase price.Preserving a piece of Old HollywoodThe estate measures approximately 4,585 square feet and sits on a half-acre lot. Its two-story main residence and guesthouse provide five bedrooms and seven bathrooms, while a room currently used as a gym offers the possibility of creating an additional bedroom.The layout includes a distinctive connection between the primary suite and the guesthouse through a concealed closet. The guesthouse also has its own entrance, giving it a degree of independence from the main residence.Inside, the property features spacious living areas, a home office with a fireplace and built-in bookshelves, and a kitchen with an island and breakfast nook. Large windows and glass doors connect the interiors with the surrounding gardens, allowing natural light to filter through the house.The grounds are equally central to the property’s appeal. A kidney-shaped swimming pool and adjoining deck overlook the canyon and cityscape, with views extending towards Catalina Island on clear days. A trail from the property also provides direct access to Fryman Canyon, a popular hiking destination in the Santa Monica Mountains.The estate’s relatively intact period character is particularly notable in a neighbourhood where older homes have frequently been replaced by larger, contemporary constructions. Its history, combined with its established landscaping and hillside setting, gives it a different appeal from the newer luxury properties that dominate much of the local market.From a $2.8 million purchase to a $6.5 million listingGuza and Bennett purchased the house in 2003 for approximately $2.8 million, according to a contemporaneous Los Angeles Times real estate report published on June 29 that year. The report also documented the property’s earlier connections to Peck and Karloff, establishing its celebrity history well before the current listing.The couple’s purchase was motivated in part by the home’s access to hiking trails. Bennett, who worked in television and had previously acted, and Guza subsequently maintained their connection to the property for more than two decades. The current $6.5 million asking price represents an increase of approximately $3.7 million over the reported 2003 purchase price, or around 132%. That is a nominal comparison and does not account for inflation, maintenance, improvements or other ownership costs.The property was listed in July 2026, according to real estate records and the listing information published by Mansion Global and property platforms including Zillow. Its combination of celebrity provenance, preserved architecture and canyon-facing grounds places it among the more distinctive historic homes currently being offered in Beverly Hills. For prospective buyers, the appeal extends beyond the names associated with its past. The house offers an opportunity to own a surviving example of the residential architecture and Hollywood culture that helped define the area more than eight decades ago.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: GOP senator calls for FCC probe of ABC News over Trump sons-Anduril 'political hit job'
articles.summary: Sen. Bernie Moreno urged the FCC to investigate ABC News over a retracted report linking Donald Trump Jr. and Anduril Industries to government contracts.
articles.body: Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-OH, called on the Federal Communications Commission on Saturday to launch a formal investigation into ABC News after the network deleted and substantially revised a report involving President Donald Trump's sons and defense contractor Anduril Industries, accusing the Disney-owned network of publishing false information that could damage a major investment in his home state. In a letter to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, Moreno demanded accountability for the network's report and questioned whether ABC News violated its obligations as a broadcaster. "Thus, I urge the Commission to open a formal investigation into ABC News's political hit job. We must know who signed off on the publication of this false story, who may have asked to profit from the attack, and whether ABC News's conduct violated its obligations as a licensee," Moreno said. Fox News Digital reached out to Moreno's office for additional comment but a spokesperson for the senator declined to elaborate on the allegations. FCC CALLS IN DISNEY-OWNED ABC STATIONS FOR EARLY LICENSE REVIEW IN WAKE OF JIMMY KIMMEL CONTROVERSY The senator's request followed ABC News' decision to remove a report examining investments tied to Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump. The original Wednesday article claimed companies connected to the president's sons had secured billions in government contracts, including through venture capital firm 1789 Capital. Moreno specifically challenged the original report's characterization of Anduril's financing, arguing that the network had misrepresented the company's investment activity and unfairly associated the Trump family with federal contracting decisions. "ABC News appears under broadcast licenses issued by the FCC. These licenses are a privilege, not a right. They require service of the public interest," he said. FCC BOSS BRENDAN CARR MAINTAINS EARLY ABC LICENSE RENEWAL IS ABOUT DEI PROBE, NOT JIMMY KIMMEL CONTROVERSY The controversy centered on ABC News' original claim that 1789 Capital, where Trump Jr. serves as a partner, acquired a major strike in Anduril through a $2.5 billion investment. The figure instead represented Anduril's broader fundraising round, while 1789 Capital's investment was approximately $50 million. ABC News republished a substantially revised article Friday, acknowledging errors involving investments, government contracts and the chronology of events. The updated version also clarified that Trump Jr. does not serve on the firm's investment decision-making committee. The report was republished Friday with a new headline, revised byline and an editor's note acknowledging factual errors involving company investments, government contracts and the chronology of events. Moreno also emphasized the economic stakes for Ohio, where Anduril is developing its Arsenal-1 manufacturing facility. The company has announced plans to invest nearly $1 billion in the project, which is expected to create more than 4,000 jobs. DISNEY SUES FCC OVER ‘RETALIATORY CAMPAIGN AGAINST ABC,’ SEEKS TO BLOCK EARLY RENEWAL PROCEEDINGS In his letter, Moreno accused ABC News of undermining public confidence in journalism while potentially harming a major employer in the state. "The American people, and the workers in Ohio whose jobs were put at risk by this reporting, deserve answers and accountability," Moreno said. The investigation request comes amid an ongoing legal dispute between Disney and the FCC over the commission's early review of ABC-owned television station licenses. Disney argued that the review threatens constitutionally protected editorial independence, while the FCC defended its actions as regulatory oversight. A network source for ABC News told Fox News Digital, "We always review every situation in a thorough and thoughtful manner and will not be providing further comment at this time."

articles.title: Dozens of gold prospectors killed in strikes on Egypt-Sudan border, rights group says
articles.summary: Neither Egypt nor Sudan has commented on the alleged strikes on an artisanal mining camp on Saturday.
articles.body:
At least 72 civilians who had been prospecting for gold in a border region of Sudan have been killed in air strikes, a regional rights group says.

Emergency Lawyers, based in the Sudanese capital, Khartoum, said jets targeted the so-called artisanal miners at a popular gold mining sites in Sudan's River Nile state on Saturday.

Neither the Egyptian government nor the de facto Sudanese authorities have so far commented.

Cairo has previously faced accusations of deadly strikes on gold prospectors as part of a crackdown on illicit activity along its southern border.

Emergency Lawyers noted the previous alleged attacks and said they represented not only a violation of Sudan's sovereign territory but demonstrated the government's lack of control over the region.

"The deliberate targeting of unarmed civilians violates international humanitarian law and the right to life," it said in a statement on Sunday. "These acts may constitute war crimes."

It noted that its death toll was provisional and could rise.

The Paris-based Sudan Tribune reported that the death toll could far exceed the number reported by Emergency Lawyers, citing a survivor of Saturday's attack who said many more people had been injured.

Eyewitnesses said the attack began around 06:00 local time (04:00 GMT), with the aircraft firing more than five missiles directly at the miners' camps, destroying them and excavation pits with people still inside, the newspaper wrote.

The Sudan Tribune reported claims in June that Egyptian forces had used drones and artillery to target artisanal mining sites in the same region, killing several, after sporadic incidents of Egyptian border guards of burning equipment, torching temporary shelters, and firing live ammunition to disperse mine workers.

Days later, Egypt's border agency announced that it and the military had begun a sweeping security campaign along the border to foil illegal migration, drug smuggling and illegal mining.

At the same time, Sudan's de facto leader announced an investigation into the alleged strikes, which were said to have killed dozens.

Gold lies at the core of the border tensions.

Sudan's ongoing civil war has led to a surge in artisanal mining - an often risky practice conducted by civilians with rudimentary tools and without official permission - particularly in remote areas near its borders.

Gold-rich areas such as those in River Nile state lie along porous borders in terrain historically associated with cross-border smuggling routes, with artisanally mined gold potentially feeding into those channels.

Egypt's border force said in June that it had seized 86 tonnes of gold ore along with amateur prospecting equipment.

Artisanal mining has also reportedly continued in Sudan's conflict zones and smuggled gold may be a source of income for armed insurgent groups.

This has raised concerns of illicit Sudanese gold undermining the legitimate Egyptian gold market.

articles.title: Reform would suspend asylum system for parliamentary term if in government
articles.summary: All asylum applications would be rejected and existing ones voided, with all claimants marked for deportation.
articles.body:
Reform UK has announced plans to close down the UK's asylum system for a full parliamentary term if it were to enter government.

The party said all new asylum applications would be rejected and existing applications voided, with all claimants marked for deportation, which Reform said would effectively suspend the asylum system.

Reform would scrap the asylum tribunal system, which hears asylum appeal cases, and claimants in more than 90,000 outstanding appeals would be deported.

It said no grants of humanitarian protection or refugee status would be made.

Labour chairperson Bridget Phillipson called the proposals a "clear sign of desperation and weakness".

"Running away from basic decency by entirely abandoning those escaping war and persecution might look to Reform like a way of winning a bidding war with other parties on the right, but the vast majority of British people will reject it as an assault on our common values," she said.

Conservative shadow home secretary Chris Philp said the proposals "largely copy" his party's policies, arguing: "Only the Conservatives have a serious and credible plan to fix our borders."

Liberal Democrat home affairs spokesperson Max Wilkinson said: "Reform and the Conservatives were the architects of the failed asylum system and now they will exploit it at every opportunity - including Farage's latest announcement."

Reform said it would pull the UK out of the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR), repeal the Human Rights Act 1998 and disapply the 1951 Refugee Convention to prevent legal challenges to its plans.

Party leader Nigel Farage said the UK is "facing a national security emergency" and "we cannot accept more asylum seekers while we still have no idea how many people are in the country illegally and the threat they pose."

Home Office staff who currently oversee asylum claims would be "reprioritised to reviewing and overturning previous refugee grants", Reform added.

The party said it would attempt to pressure other countries into accepting those marked for deportation from the UK by using visa bans and tariffs on goods and services.

Pakistan, Somalia, Eritrea, Syria, Afghanistan and Sudan could be hit with visa bans under these measures.

If these policies are unsuccessful, Reform would "apply further sanctions, including banning a country's airlines from British airspace and their citizens from transit", the announcement added.

In "extreme cases" where no country is willing to take custody of a deportee or it is inappropriate to return someone to their home country, Reform said it would negotiate deals with third countries.

In April, Reform pledged an immediate review of all asylum claims from the last five years should the party win the next general election.

Around 400,000 people would be liable for deportation under the plans, which would target anybody granted asylum, overstaying a visa, or from a country deemed safe by a Reform-led government.

The party previously announced it would bar anyone arriving on a small boat, and suggested this could mean 600,000 deportations over five years.

Both Labour and the Conservatives have also pledged to make changes to the asylum system.

Phillipson said Farage is "casting around for more and more extreme policies" as he deals with questions about finances and rival party Restore Britain.

Phillipson said Labour is showing "we can control immigration and get numbers down with serious action, not by abandoning the asylum system altogether", adding the "right approach" is "not giving up or caving to the most extreme voices, but ensuring that the rules we have are properly enforced".

In March, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said any asylum seeker given refugee status will now only be offered temporary protection, reviewed every 30 months.

In September, she also reopened a scheme to resettle refugees in the UK, saying she hoped that offering "safe and legal" routes would deter small boat crossings.

The Home Office said the UK Resettlement Scheme (UKRS) would reopen immediately and expected that around 25% of arrivals would be Afghan women and girls and Palestinians.

Philp said Reform's plans mostly mirror Conservative policy from a year ago, including banning asylum claims by people who entered the country illegally, abolishing the immigration tribunal, ending Labour's resettlement routes, and leaving the ECHR.

The Tories previously said they would task officials with removing 750,000 illegal immigrants within five years, under Trump-style deportation plans.

Lib Dems spokesperson Wilkinson said the "UK can only restore order, control and fairness by joining the EU migration and asylum pact", which increases the number of irregular migrants returned to their home countries and spreads responsibility for asylum seekers across the EU.

articles.title: Ann Rutherford’s 1938 Beverly Hills estate was bought for about $7.6 million in 2013 and nearly doubled in size; after selling for $27.6 million, the Paul R. Williams-designed home is back on the market for $35 million
articles.summary: A historic Beverly Hills mansion once owned by Gone With the Wind actress Ann Rutherford has returned to the market for $35 million, nearly eight years
articles.body: A historic Beverly Hills mansion once owned by Gone With the Wind actress Ann Rutherford has returned to the market for $35 million, nearly eight years after its last recorded sale for $27.625 million. The property, known as the Rutherford House, is listed at 826 Greenway Drive and combines the architectural legacy of Paul R. Williams with extensive renovations and contemporary luxury. According to property records published by Zillow and Realtor.com, the estate was relisted on August 20, 2026, following earlier listing attempts at higher prices. Mansion Global previously reported its 2018 sale and the renovation that substantially expanded the house.A Hollywood legacy with a distinctive architectural identityCompleted in 1938, the French Revival-style residence was originally built for Edward Paul Dentzel, a Beverly Hills mayor and real estate developer. Rutherford, known for her role as Carreen O’Hara in the 1939 film Gone With the Wind, later lived at the property with her husband, William Dozier, the television producer behind the 1960s Batman series.The couple’s association with the mansion extended beyond its address. The estate reportedly hosted several weddings, earning it the nickname Greenway Chapel, according to Mansion Global’s 2025 coverage of the property. Its history as a gathering place for Hollywood figures remains part of its appeal.Inside the $35 million estateThe latest listing describes a five-bedroom residence spanning approximately 13,678 square feet on a lot measuring about 26,743 square feet. Property records and earlier coverage give different figures for the home’s interior area, reflecting its substantial renovation and differences in published measurements.The interiors retain a formal, period-inspired character while incorporating modern amenities. A grand entrance opens to a winding staircase, with formal living and dining rooms setting the tone. The house also features a library inspired by French designer Émile-Jacques Ruhlmann, a billiards room, a bar and a morning room decorated with historic wallpaper and an original fireplace.The kitchen pairs marble finishes and a mosaic-tiled ceiling with contemporary appliances. The primary suite includes marble bathrooms, generous closets and a separate lounge overlooking the landscaped grounds. Outside, a manicured garden surrounds an oval swimming pool, pavilion and pool house. The design draws on Williams’ architectural influence, linking the grounds to the estate’s broader emphasis on classical proportions and indoor-outdoor living.The architect behind the mansionThe property’s appeal also rests on the legacy of Paul R. Williams, one of Los Angeles’ most influential architects. During a career spanning five decades, he designed thousands of buildings, including residences for Hollywood stars and landmark projects associated with the Beverly Hills Hotel.As the Los Angeles Times has documented, Williams became the first Black architect admitted to the American Institute of Architects and built a distinguished career despite the racial discrimination that restricted where he could live and work. His residential designs were celebrated for their adaptability, elegance and attention to detail.That history gives the Rutherford House significance beyond its current asking price. It represents a period when Beverly Hills was emerging as a centre of Hollywood glamour, while reflecting the work of an architect whose influence continues to shape the city’s built environment.From a $7.6 million purchase to a $35 million asking priceThe estate changed hands in 2013 for approximately $7.75 million, according to Zillow’s recorded sales history. The buyers undertook extensive renovations, expanding the home from roughly 5,800 square feet, as reported by Mansion Global in 2018.The renovated property subsequently entered the market at $39.9 million in 2017 before selling for $27.625 million in December 2018. It returned to the market in July 2025 at $42 million, followed by another listing at $39.5 million in February 2026. After that listing was withdrawn, the asking price was reset to $35 million in August, according to Zillow and Realtor.com.The current price remains well above the estate’s 2013 purchase price, although an asking price does not establish the amount a buyer will ultimately pay. For now, the Rutherford House is being marketed as a rare combination of classic Hollywood history, a major architectural pedigree and an extensively updated Beverly Hills residence.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Three men found guilty of murdering Australian brothers and American friend on Mexico surfing trip
articles.summary: Prosecutors are seeking 210 years in prison for each defendant convicted in the murders of the Australian brothers and their American friend.
articles.body: Three men have been convicted in the brutal killings of two Australian brothers and their American friend, whose disappearance on a Mexico surf trip sparked an international search before their bodies were found dumped in a well. A judge in Ensenada on Friday found Jesús Gerardo García, known as "El Kekas," Irineo Francisco "N," and Ángel Jesús "N," guilty of murdering Callum and Jake Robinson, along with their friend Carter Rhoad, in Baja, California, in April 2024, The Associated Press reported. The men were also convicted of armed robbery and armed carjacking. Judge Raúl Hernández is scheduled to announce their sentences Oct. 16, with the Baja California State Attorney General’s Office seeking 210 years in prison for each defendant, according to the AP. MINNESOTA FATHER CONVICTED OF KILLING TEENAGE SON WHOSE REMAINS WERE FOUND IN LANDFILL The verdicts followed a month-long trial that included testimony about one victim pleading for his life before the killings. García’s former partner, Ary Gisell Silva Raya, testified that he told her he approached the surfers’ tent carrying a 9mm pistol, the AP reported. The men threw their belongings toward him in an effort to stop the attack, and one begged to be spared, she said. AMERICAN AIRLINES FLIGHT ATTENDANT'S ALLEGED KILLERS TIED TO GANG ACCUSED OF PREYING ON TOURISTS: OFFICIALS According to her testimony, García ignored the plea. The friends had traveled to Baja, California, to surf and were reported missing after arriving in Punta San Jose, about 50 miles from Ensenada. Their bodies were discovered in a well May 3, 2024. MEXICAN SPORTS JOURNALIST ROBBED AT GUNPOINT DURING LIVE REPORT Authorities initially said the men were killed after confronting thieves who wanted the tires from their pickup truck. Chief state prosecutor María Elena Andrade Ramírez said at the time that investigators believed the thieves spotted the truck and tents, then encountered resistance from the surfers during the attempted theft. García allegedly told his girlfriend he had done something to "three gringos" before admitting, "I killed them," according to the BBC’s account of a May 2024 court hearing. She also said he showed her a vehicle fitted with tires allegedly stolen from the victims’ truck. MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING PARTNER ARRESTED IN MEXICO NEARLY TWO YEARS AFTER FLEEING WITH THEIR TWO CHILDREN Silva Raya was found with one victim’s cellphone. Prosecutors said she met the surfers April 27, 2024, and urged one of her companions to rob them, the AP reported. She pleaded guilty to aggravated robbery with violence and vehicle theft with violence and was sentenced to 20 years in prison in November 2025. García and the other two men went to trial. JURY CONVICTS KEVIN SALAZAR IN EXECUTION-STYLE KILLING OF LA DEPUTY RYAN CLINKUNBROOMER The guilty verdicts brought a measure of relief to the Robinson family more than two years after the brothers’ deaths. Their father, Martin Robinson, described the decision as a significant moment in the family’s painful pursuit of justice, according to the AP. He said the outcome could not undo their loss but offered a step toward justice as they continued honoring the three men. MAN PLEADS GUILTY TO 2023 KILLING OF LAUREN HEIKE ON PHOENIX HIKING TRAIL The brothers’ mother, Debra Robinson, spoke about their love of surfing during a tribute on a San Diego beach shortly after their bodies were found. "Our hearts are broken, and the world has become a darker place for us," she said at the time. "They were young men enjoying their passion of surfing together." She recalled that Jake, a doctor, sought work at hospitals near surfing beaches and urged others to honor her sons by embracing life. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Live bigger, shine brighter, and love harder in their memory," she said. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Trump Russia deal could fuel Putin's war, ex-NATO commander warns as Zelenskyy says 'nyet'
articles.summary: Donald Trump's energy ceasefire could hand Vladimir Putin fresh revenue to fuel Russia's war in Ukraine, former NATO commander Breedlove warns.
articles.body: President Donald Trump's efforts to reach a diesel agreement with Russia could provide Russian President Vladimir Putin with fresh revenue to fund his war against Ukraine while allowing Moscow to buy time through negotiations it has little intention of honoring, a former NATO commander warned Sunday. Retired Gen. Philip Breedlove, former NATO supreme allied commander Europe and head of U.S. European Command, told Fox News Digital that Washington also risks undermining Ukraine's war effort by striking a deal with what he called "the enemy." "And so we are cutting a deal with the enemy," Breedlove said, warning that "all of this money will go into fueling Mr. Putin's continued attacks in Ukraine." The Russian government said Saturday it had partially lifted a ban on diesel exports with immediate effect, following the new agreement between Putin and Trump for Russia to supply the U.S. and global markets, Reuters reported. As previously reported by Fox News Digital, Trump's package calls for the release of 300,000 tonnes of diesel "to the American and global marketplace," followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and another 1 million tonnes afterward. KATIE ZACHARIA HITS GROUND RUNNING, PROMISES TRUMP DIESEL DEAL DELIVERS CHEAPER GAS FOR AMERICANS The diesel agreement preceded Trump's announcement Sunday of what he called an "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine, with the president saying both sides had agreed to halt attacks on energy infrastructure. "Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!" Trump wrote on Truth Social. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, however, indicated that Ukraine had not been informed of a finalized ceasefire agreement but expressed willingness to halt attacks on Russian energy facilities if Moscow reciprocated. He also accused Putin of repeatedly rejecting peace proposals and continuing strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure. "Ukraine has proposed many de-escalatory steps. Putin had one answer to all of them – 'nyet,'" Zelenskyy wrote on X. "We do hope that he will finally say something to America, Ukraine, and the entire world that will lead to a real and dignified peace," he added. Zelenskyy also said Russian forces had carried out more than 200 strikes on Ukraine's electricity generation and transmission facilities over the past week, along with 17 strikes targeting gas and oil infrastructure. He said the attacks had killed more than 150 people and wounded more than 700 over the past week. Trump's "energy ceasefire" announcement followed tension between Washington and Kyiv over Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries, a component of Ukraine's strategy to weaken Moscow's ability to finance its military campaign. UKRAINE TARGETS RUSSIA WITH OVER 1,000 DRONES, KILLING 2 AS MOSCOW HOLDS LAST DAY OF ELECTIONS Breedlove argued that Russia and Ukraine are pursuing different objectives, accusing Moscow of targeting Ukrainian civilians and critical infrastructure while describing Kyiv's attacks on Russian energy facilities as an effort to disrupt the revenue sustaining Putin's war. "Russia is carrying on a campaign of what we call counter value. In other words, Russia is attacking the Ukrainian people and trying to force their society to separate themselves from their president, President Zelenskyy," Breedlove said. Breedlove also predicted Washington would pressure Zelenskyy to suspend attacks on Russia's oil industry despite their strategic importance. "What I expect will happen is the United States will force or try to force Zelenskyy to stop bombing the petrochemical business in Russia," he said. TRUMP'S DIESEL IDEA COULD HAVE UNLEASHED A PROBLEM AMERICANS NEVER SAW COMING Trump has vehemently criticized Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries, arguing that they are disrupting global diesel supplies and driving up costs for American farmers and ranchers. Meanwhile, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent defended the administration's efforts to increase diesel supplies. "We're going to do it with all the legal authorities we have," Bessent said Sunday on Fox News. "This is good for the American people, bringing these diesel prices down," he said of the new deal. Separately, appearing on ABC News' "This Week," Zelenskyy offered to organize Ukrainian elections if Putin agreed to a reciprocal 60-day ceasefire, although holding a vote would face legal and logistical obstacles under Ukraine's martial law. Breedlove also expressed deep skepticism that Putin would honor any such ceasefire, citing what he described as a pattern of Russian attacks following negotiations with Trump. "Russia has never kept a promise to this president in this war," Breedlove said. UKRAINE'S ATTACKS ON RUSSIA ARE PUSHING PUTIN CLOSER TO NEGOTIATING TABLE, TRUMP NATO AMBASSADOR SAYS "He's never changed his expectations, and he's never delivered on his promises. Three out of four of the big cases, the very next day or that same night after the president and Mr. Putin talked, Mr. Putin launched huge attacks in Ukraine," Breedlove continued. Breedlove also called for a tougher U.S. response. "We now need an administration that leads from power. We say all the time, 'strength through power,' but when it comes to Russia, our demonstrated position is continued conflict through weakness," Breedlove warned. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "He started this war. This war is to benefit Russia, and this war is to keep Mr. Putin in power. And our administration needs to tell him to stop."

articles.title: Bangladesh party backs CJP stir, ex-Yunus aide seeks Modi's fall
articles.summary: DHAKA: Hardline Jamaat-e-Islami ally and NCP convener Nahid Islam, a key member of the July 2024 movement that led to Sheikh Hasina's ouster as Bangladesh
articles.body: DHAKA: Hardline Jamaat-e-Islami ally and NCP convener Nahid Islam, a key member of the July 2024 movement that led to Sheikh Hasina's ouster as Bangladesh PM, backed the CJP-spearheaded protests in New Delhi, while a former adviser to the erstwhile Muhammad Yunus-led interim govt said he was waiting to witness PM Narendra Modi's downfall."The struggles of young people in Bangladesh and India are interconnected," said the convener of National Citizen Party. Young Indians are demanding electoral accountability and the protection of democratic rights, he said and asked them to "stand firm, protect one another, reject communal hatred, and refuse to surrender the future of South Asia to fascism and division"."To the democratic people of India: from Dhaka, and from the unfinished democratic aspirations of our July generation, we stand with you," Islam, who is also opposition chief whip in the Bangladesh parliament, said in a statement on X Saturday. "Hindutva majoritarianism, fascism and religious supremacy should not shape South Asia's future."He was joined by Asif Nazrul, who said, "The people of this country have suffered in various ways, falling victim to Modi and his politics; they and their families will find some solace.""Like many others, I, too, am waiting to witness Modi's downfall," said the former adviser to the interim govt under which Bangladesh-India bilateral ties nosedived.If Modi govt fell, things would change - anti-Muslim politics would suffer a setback, Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu would lose an ally and inequalities in society might be diminished, he said, adding Modi was facing pressure from "cockroach bites".Islam stressed the stud-ent-led movement against recruitment quotas had developed into an uprising against 15 years of "authoritarian rule" in Bangladesh. He brought up India's history of "democratic resistance", citing the Shaheen Bagh protests and student activism at JNU and Jadavpur University."This struggle is not yours alone. From Dhaka, we stand with you as friends bound by a common demand for accountable power, democratic institutions, and human dignity," he said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 2022, Ryan Reynolds and Blake Lively gave $500,000 to Water First; four years later, the Canadian charity's latest graduating class included eight newly certified Indigenous water operators
articles.summary: In 2022, Ryan Reynolds and Blake Lively donated $500,000 to Water First, a Canadian charity that works with Indigenous communities on water education and
articles.body: In 2022, Ryan Reynolds and Blake Lively donated $500,000 to Water First, a Canadian charity that works with Indigenous communities on water education and training. Four years later, the organisation marked a milestone: eight Indigenous trainees had graduated from a 15-month programme as certified water operators. The graduates completed more than 2,000 hours of hands-on training and passed the exams required for certification, according to Water First. Their achievement points to the long-term purpose of the 2022 gift, which was intended to help more Indigenous young adults train for water-related careers. The donation did not solve Canada’s drinking-water challenges on its own, but it supported a locally focused approach: building skills so communities can strengthen their own capacity to manage water systems.A donation aimed at local trainingWhen Reynolds and Lively announced their donation in March 2022, they said it would support Water First’s education and training programmes for Indigenous youth and young adults. The funds were intended to help train water treatment plant operators and environmental water science technicians, as well as introduce school-aged students to water science. Reynolds described access to clean drinking water as a basic human right and said the couple valued Water First’s focus on training Indigenous adults to become certified operators and technicians. Their contribution supported a charity that works alongside communities to develop programmes shaped by local priorities, rather than relying on a single, identical solution for every place, as per the report.Water First says its partnerships are built around collaboration with Indigenous communities. Local leaders help identify needs and shape the training, with the goal of developing expertise within the communities themselves. That approach recognises that the challenges facing one water system may differ from those affecting another.The need for trained local operators is one part of a wider picture. Communities can face issues involving infrastructure, water quality or a shortage of people qualified to operate treatment systems. Training does not replace necessary equipment or investment, but it can help communities build the people and knowledge needed to manage water systems over the long term.Eight new operators graduateThe latest group of graduates completed a Drinking Water Internship run through a partnership between Water First, the Anishinaabeg of Kabapikotawangag Resource Council, participating communities and Big Island First Nation. The eight graduates celebrated their achievement in May 2026. The 15-month programme combined classroom learning with practical experience. Each intern completed more than 2,000 hours of hands-on training and wrote four exams required to earn Water Operator certification. The work prepared participants for the responsibilities involved in operating drinking-water treatment systems. The graduates are now equipped to pursue careers in water treatment and related environmental fields. Their training can also benefit their communities directly, particularly where local residents are needed to operate and maintain water facilities.One graduate, Brandon Penner of Big Grassy First Nation, said the programme pushed him beyond his comfort zone and helped him recognise what he could achieve through commitment. He also spoke of a deep connection to the natural world and a desire to protect it for future generations.Why local operators matterFor many communities, having trained local people involved in water management can make a difference to both daily operations and long-term self-sufficiency. Water First’s announcement quoted Rhonda Nash, director of operations at AKRC, saying that certified operators were needed for the council’s five member First Nations, which include seven separate communities, two of them remote. Nash said the goal was to ensure access to clean drinking water while creating employment and enabling community members to operate their own treatment plants. The model links technical training with local jobs and community capacity.That work is important because water systems require skilled people to monitor processes, respond to problems and maintain consistent operations. The graduates’ certification gives them a professional foundation, while their local knowledge and relationships can help connect technical work with community needs.Water First says its internship alumni can also access continuing career development and education through an expanding professional network. That support matters because training is not a one-time event. Operators may need ongoing learning as their responsibilities grow and water-management challenges change.A continuing water challengeThe graduation comes amid persistent drinking-water concerns in Indigenous communities across Canada. Water First’s May 2026 release said 16% of First Nations were affected by a drinking-water advisory, with the figure rising to 32% in Ontario. The charity cautioned that the issue is complex, involving different combinations of infrastructure, source-water quality and staffing needs.Those figures help explain why the organisation focuses on partnerships and locally designed programmes. No single intervention can address every cause of unsafe or unreliable water. Communities may need infrastructure improvements, source-water protection, technical expertise and sustained funding, often at the same time.Water First frames training as one part of the solution, not a substitute for broader action. Developing local expertise can help communities operate systems and strengthen their ability to respond to challenges, while wider infrastructure and policy needs remain.Building skills for the long termThe eight new operators are part of a growing network. Water First reported that 73 interns from 47 Indigenous communities had graduated from its internship programmes to date, logging approximately 170,000 hours working in local water plants and attending workshops.Those numbers represent more than training hours. They reflect the development of experience that can remain within communities and support future generations. A certified operator can help a community manage a water system today, while also becoming a mentor or resource for others pursuing similar work.Reynolds and Lively’s $500,000 donation helped Water First expand its capacity to offer hands-on training to more Indigenous youth and adults. Four years later, the graduation of eight operators shows one concrete outcome of that broader effort. The donation was one contribution among many, alongside funding from government programmes, community partnerships and other supporters.The water challenges facing Indigenous communities are far from resolved. But the new graduates represent an important step towards local capacity, skilled employment and stronger community involvement in water management. Their certification gives them tools to protect a resource that communities depend on every day, and helps keep the work of building a more sustainable future close to home.You use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress, which had planned a march to Supreme Court for a meeting with CJI Surya Kant on the SIR-CEC issue Monday, could be forced to engineer
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress, which had planned a march to Supreme Court for a meeting with CJI Surya Kant on the SIR-CEC issue Monday, could be forced to engineer another protest programme, with the CJI turning down its request for appointment late Sunday.The Congress brass could reiterate its request for a meeting Monday.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge had posted on X that a meeting was scheduled, leading many in the opposition, including legal eagles, to express surprise, saying it would be a first-of-its-kind meet, if it happened.Rahul Gandhi cancelled a campaign event in Goa and returned home after "chhatron ki goonj" in Chennai to oversee the preparations for a massive protest that Congress has planned. He issued a general appeal to citizens, opposition parties and civil society to join the march to SC, saying Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Ajit Doval and Mohan Bhagwat could not "silence India's voice".Rahul said on X that the "March for Democracy - Dilli Chalo" will start from Barakhambha Road, and has asked people to assemble there.Slamming the police crackdown on protests, Kharge said what is happening in the capital under the Modi govt did not happen during the Emergency. "We will apprise the CJI of the situation. We cannot demand anything from him, but we will place our concerns before him with folded hands and request his intervention," he had said, adding that he and Rahul have written to CJI.Sources had said the letter to the CJI detailed the key points of the memorandum to be submitted to him, as well as the police crackdown and harassment of protesters by vigilantes.AICC general secretary KC Venugopal asked party workers from all states to converge in the capital for the mega surge. State presidents, including Rao Narender of Haryana, Ganesh Godiyal of Uttarakhand and Govind Dotasara of Rajasthan, issued instructions to party workers to leave for Delhi in large numbers - an indication of the kind of mobilisation the opposition party has set rolling.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: CJI: No meet with Congress, it'll violate 'separation of power'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: CJI Surya Kant Sunday declined requests from Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and MP Rahul Gandhi, who wanted to meet him Monday to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: CJI Surya Kant Sunday declined requests from Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and MP Rahul Gandhi, who wanted to meet him Monday to apprise him about "vote chori" allegations amid protests in Delhi seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.In an email response, the CJI said similar issues were already pending adjudication before Supreme Court and a meeting on the issue raised by the netas would "contravene the iconic principles of separation of power, which is part of the basic structure of Constitution", sources in the CJI office told TOI.The response said SC was not endowed with any administrative power in this regard and only had an adjudicatory role under Constitution. It said the party or any of its functionaries could file a petition highlighting their grievances and the court was bound to adjudicate it. The sources said the CJI stated that SC was committed to giving a priority hearing to important issues and serving citizens of the country.The sources said the CJI wrote that if so advised, a petition could be filed by the person concerned or the party in SC before 4pm Monday, and would be given priority hearing on the judicial side along with other similar petitions.Kharge, in a social media post Sunday, said, "We will continue our fight. Tomorrow, we are also going to meet CJI. I have written a letter, and Rahul Gandhi has also written a letter. We have scheduled a meeting between 4-5pm, during which we will apprise him of the situation... Chaos is being created in the country by home minister and PM, and everywhere an undeclared emergency is imposed."Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Protests against SIR-CEC intensify, several detained in Mumbai, Pune
articles.summary: Protests backing Cockroach Janta Party's crusade against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and SIR intensified Sunday across several states, with
articles.body: Protests backing Cockroach Janta Party's crusade against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and SIR intensified Sunday across several states, with Sena UBT's Aaditya Thackeray and MNS's Amit Thackeray spearheading demonstrations in Mumbai.Mumbai's Shivaji Park turned into a cauldron of heaving agitators, slogans and cheek-by-jowl police deployments. The cousins slammed the "cowardly" and "dictatorial" BJP govt and sought the release of those detained.Near Shiv Sena Bhavan, Amit climbed onto a police van to announce before large crowds that the protests would intensify from Monday.Aaditya called the situation an "undeclared Emergency". He said, "It is BJP versus Bharat. The agitation will continue till CEC Gyanesh Kumar resigns." Aaditya claimed the Centre had put more forces in Delhi than it had during the Kargil War. "Why is BSF in Delhi, deployed against Indian citizens?" he said.Activist Anjali Damania was among dozens detained at Shivaji Park.In Pune, 85 CJP protesters were detained. One agitator urged govt not to "act like a dictator" and demanded SIR be scrapped.In Goa, CJP, backed by the Enough is Enough movement, organised a protest in Panaji. Police detained seven, including councillor corporator Jack Sukhija. A habeas corpus petition in the HC led to an urgent hearing Sunday, with orders for their release.In Hyderabad, 100 protesters gathered at Dharna Chowk. Among those present were M Ranga Sai Reddy and Rajesh Korapaka, Telangana CJP members detained in Bhopal recently while on their way to Delhi. "Cops had pictures of us," said Korapaka.In Kolkata, Mamata Banerjee's TMC, Congress and CPM demanded fresh elections in Bengal. MP Saugata Roy said the opposition would impeach the CEC but "a mass movement must be built before that happens".BJP dismissed the agitations. "In India, there's a fashion among certain people to hold protests," Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh said. He also mocked the former CM, who is in Delhi for the protests, saying she "should join a movement in Bangladesh".In Congress-governed Keralam, the assembly is set to adopt a resolution Monday to restore voters excluded in SIR and remove the CEC. With Left supporting the resolution, its passage is certain.Bengaluru saw at least 300 demonstrators at Freedom Park. "Asking questions isn't anarchy. Abusing power is," a placard read.(With inputs from Ahmed Ali, Priyanka Kakodkar, Chaitanya Marpakwar, Prasad Kulkarni, Gitesh Shelke, Sakshat Tornekar, Srishti Lakhotia, Chethan Kumar, Anush S & agencies)Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Government slams UN rights body for 'practising double standards'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Amid the clampdown in Delhi, Indian govt for the second time in two days slammed Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR)
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Amid the clampdown in Delhi, Indian govt for the second time in two days slammed Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) for raising concerns about mass detentions in the city, saying this constituted an unacceptable interference in India's internal affairs.While Indian mission to UN in Geneva said Saturday Indian citizens exercise their right to peaceful assembly subject to "reasonable restrictions" in the interest of public order, the ministry of external affairs tweaked the phrasing to "maintenance of public order and safety".Govt also accused the UN human rights office of practising double standards, alluding to the crackdown in PoK, saying this erodes the credibility of its standing and contributes to loss of faith in multilateralism."We also note OHCHR has an approach of extreme selectivity when it comes to public positions. Violent responses to protests in our neighbourhood have gone uncommented, as indeed have law enforcement actions in its own vicinity," said MEA, also referring to action in countries like France, Belgium and Germany without naming them.The UN body had urged Indian authorities to release all those detained.The MEA said India is the world's largest democracy, where the right to peaceful assembly is guaranteed by Constitution and safeguarded by robust institutions, an independent judiciary and a free media."As in every democracy, Indian citizens exercise this right subject to the maintenance of public order... Our law enforcement authorities act strictly in accordance with the law, and our courts remain available to all for the redressal of any grievances," it said, adding OHCHR's concerns were unwarranted.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Childhood cancer symptoms - what to look out for
articles.summary: Although rare, cancer is the leading cause of death from disease among children under 15 in the UK.
articles.body:
Although rare, cancer is the leading cause of death from disease among children under 15 in the UK - yet just under a third of parents say they feel confident recognising the symptoms.

About 1,900 children aged 0-14 are diagnosed with cancer each year, according to Cancer Research UK.

Thirteen-year-old Amelia Carroll, who is now in remission, was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) last year.

Her mum Gemma recalls the initial symptoms being easy to overlook.

There was the tiredness, she says, and being out of breath after mild exercise but both were put down to being unfit and just post-school fatigue.

It was only when Amelia started presenting with bruises Gemma knew something wasn't right - within 10 days Amelia got her leukaemia diagnosis.

Prof Bob Phillips, a paediatric oncologist, says it's key for parents to look out for clusters of symptoms that may be persisting, getting worse or bigger.

Consider contacting a doctor over the following:

Lumps and bumps that are getting bigger or not going away and growing over time

Cancer in children develops much more quickly than in adults - effectively due to them growing.

Experts like Phillips at CCLG, the Children and Young People's Cancer Association, are urging people to follow a national campaign aiming to raise awareness and improve diagnosis times.

It includes a rule-of-three for professionals: If a child has had three persistent symptoms, or has visited their doctor three times, or has had three weeks of unexplained symptoms consider making a referral.

Although, it's important to note survival rates have risen significantly since the 1970s, with eight out of 10 children surviving beyond five to 10 years or more after diagnosis.

For Amelia, her cancer journey began with a single red bruise that came out of nowhere, says Gemma.

Three days later, she had bruises down both of her shins on both legs, which were sore and raised.

"We'd gone to the opticians for a routine appointment and they noticed that she'd got some burst blood vessels but they weren't sure why," she adds.

Within 10 days, doctors had confirmed what type of leukaemia Amelia had and she was admitted to hospital to begin treatment.

"On the day that they confirmed what she had, I sat her down and she said to me 'have I got cancer?' and I said yes you have. She asked me if she was going to die."

"I said no, they're doing everything they can, they've got a plan in place and the treatment is going to do everything it can to beat the cancer."

Amelia is currently in remission, undergoing regular bone marrow and blood tests every three months, and has returned to school.

Phillips says survival rates for childhood cancer in the UK are over 80% but that even quicker diagnosis would lead to less intensive treatments.

Around the UK, about half the children diagnosed with cancer get their diagnosis within two weeks, he says.

"It's pretty quick but we want the other half to not have the wait of 16, 18, 20, 25 weeks from those first symptoms to get a diagnosis."

Cancer Research UK data shows that there are more than 400,000 new cases of cancer diagnosed every year in the UK, with only 54% being told within the 28-day NHS target window, according to the British Medical Journal (BMJ).

An additional 2,300 teenagers and young adults (aged 15–24) are diagnosed each year.

Lynsey Swinscoe is mum to Jake, who died of soft tissue cancer aged 13. Jake was diagnosed with stage three, fusion positive alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma in July 2023.

Before his diagnosis, Jake's initial symptoms of a stuffy nose and watery eyes were put down to hayfever, and falling asleep after school was thought to be just end-of-term tiredness.

"It was only when he started to get a swelling across the bridge of his nose that we thought right, we need to take him to the GP," Lynsey says.

"But at that point we didn't really think the fatigue and hayfever symptoms were related."

A mass was found in Jake's nose and nasal cavity and he was diagnosed with soft tissue sarcoma. He completed nine rounds of chemotherapy and proton beam radiation.

After suffering seizures and feeling very unwell from the chemotherapy, Jake opted out of continuing treatment.

He passed away peacefully at home on 26 April 2024, just two weeks before his 14th birthday.

"I think the main thing with Jake is he was not scared to die. We had lots of conversations about dying and what it might feel like to die and the only thing that he was sort of scared about was, 'are all the people going to remember me? Is everyone just going to forget who I am?'

"That's why I'm doing this, to make sure that people know who Jake is, to make sure people know how incredible he was. And so with that comes the raising awareness, which I think, that's his legacy."

articles.title: Sacha Baron Cohen to star in Quentin Tarantino's West End play
articles.summary: The Borat star said he was "beyond delighted" to be working on the show, The Popinjay Cavalier, with the Pulp Fiction director.
articles.body:
Borat actor Sacha Baron Cohen will star in a new play in London's West End from Hollywood director Quentin Tarantino.

The Popinjay Cavalier, set in 1830s Europe, was announced earlier this year and is the first play to be written for stage by the US filmmaker, who is also set to direct.

Baron Cohen said he was "beyond delighted" to be working with Tarantino, saying: "When the best director in the world calls, you don't ask questions."

The director, best known for violent film classics Pulp Fiction and Reservoir Dogs, has said he is "keen with anticipation to give the West End a great night out".

The play is set to premiere in March next year, with tickets available from Monday.

The production was announced in March this year as a "rambunctious comedy of deception and disguise inspired by the grand swashbuckling epics of stage and screen".

Baron Cohen, 54, is known for his self-created comic characters including infamous spoof wannabe gangster Ali G , Kazakh reporter Borat Sagdiyev, and Austrian fashionista Brüno Gehard.

He has won two Baftas and three Golden Globes, as well as being nominated for three Oscars and six Emmys.

The full cast for The Popinjay Cavalier is planned to be announced at a later date.

The play will be co-produced by Sony Pictures Entertainment, which distributed Tarantino's most recent film Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood, and Sonia Friedman Productions, which has overseen hits like Harry Potter and the Cursed Child and Paddington the Musical.

The director has repeatedly spoken about planning to retire from movies after making 10 films.

He has made nine so far - he counts Kill Bill Volumes One and Two together - and has won two Oscars, for writing Pulp Fiction and Django Unchained.

Tarantino revealed his plan to stage a play last summer, telling the Church of Tarantino podcast it was "all written".

"It is absolutely the next thing I'm going to do. We'll start the ball rolling on it in January. It's probably going to take up a year and a half to two years of my life, if it's a success and I've got to do the tour version of it and all that," he said.

"I'm preparing for it to be a success. If it's a flop, I'll be done very quickly."

The Popinjay Cavalier will premiere at the Phoenix Theatre on 18 March 2027, with tickets starting from £25.

The 63-year-old director lives in Tel Aviv with his Israeli wife, Daniella Pick, and their two children. He told the podcast last year that he would "more than likely move to England and bring my family with me" while working on the play.

Tarantino is also known for his forthright personality and made headlines at the end of last year for launching a stinging criticism of actor Paul Dano, as well as in March this year for a spat with Pulp Fiction actress Rosanna Arquette after she criticised the use of the N-word in the 1994 film.
